page.title: Your food, portable.
page.purpose: Export, print, import, and restore owned data with review before write, explicit duplicate decisions, and a recoverable checkpoint, never exporting secrets or tenant authority.

priorities.statement: Export, import, and restore are named distinctly so a recipe PDF is never mistaken for a complete backup.
An import is parsed and reviewed with counts, duplicates, unsupported fields, and unresolved references before any live write.
The default action adds meals only; restoring everything requires an explicit impact preview and a recoverable checkpoint.
Secrets, credentials, infrastructure URLs, and tenant authority are excluded from every export and cannot be granted by an import.
Retrieving the user's own data never requires a paid AI provider or an additional completeness step.

states.description: The surface at rest with data present; the state a journey step assumes when it names none.
First read of the page's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
The read succeeded and there is genuinely nothing, which is distinct from not-yet-loaded.
Some contributing data could not be read; what is missing is named rather than shown as zero.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
The request failed; the reason and the next available action are stated.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified next to it.
A write is in flight; the affected control says why it is unavailable.
The client cannot reach the API; read-only or queued behavior is explained.
A parsed import is staged for review with record counts, duplicates, ID conflicts, unsupported fields, and validation paths before any write.
A full restore shows its precise impact on workspace content and the recoverable checkpoint before the explicit confirmation.

Accepts a structured file or pasted JSON; plain text is directed to Quick capture.
The staged review surface that never mutates live data during preview.
Counts by record type, source format, and version.
Keep existing, Copy incoming, or Replace with a new revision for stable-ID collisions.
Fields the target version does not support, with their paths.
Counts for removals and replacements and the workspace revision comparison.

elements.name: Restore everything
elements.description: Applies the reviewed restore transactionally after the checkpoint.
States that a recoverable pre-restore checkpoint was created.
States that secrets, credentials, and tenant authority are neither exported nor importable.
Reports export generation and download status, including a visible retry path.

claims.statement: Parsing and preview never mutate live data, and the review names counts, duplicates, unsupported fields, and validation paths first.
The default import action adds meals only, while restoring everything is a separate explicit choice.
A full restore previews removal and replacement counts and states that a recoverable checkpoint exists before the explicit confirmation.
The transfer surface states that secrets, credentials, and tenant authority are excluded from exports and cannot be installed by imports.
Exporting and printing owned data never requires a paid AI provider, extra nutrient completeness, or a subscription upgrade.
A stable-ID collision with different content offers Keep existing, Copy incoming, or Replace with a new revision, defaulting to Copy incoming with remapped references.
The grocery CSV is described as a spreadsheet view rather than a canonical lossless backup.
Export generation reports its status and offers a visible download or retry link when a browser blocks automatic saving.
The restore impact table never scrolls the whole document sideways; wide counts stay inside their region.
Unsupported fields and missing dependent records are listed in the review rather than silently dropped.
